---
title: "Drawing the chamber"
subtitle: "`src/render.ts`: two views of the colony on a canvas"
---

Drawing is kept apart from the physics: the renderer only reads the simulation through
[`forEachCell` and `forEachAnchor`](simulation.qmd#reading-the-state), plus the chamber geometry.
Either side can change without touching the other. There are two views:

- **Simple** (the default): white background; each cell's capsule outline as a thin dark line, the
  walls and wall triangles as black lines, and in red each anchor that holds a cell, as a small
  square with its spring drawn as a line to the cell's centre.
- **Diagnostic**: cells filled in their region colour with their true outlines on top, the
  material around the chamber shaded, all anchors and their springs, and overlapping cells
  highlighted: orange when deeper than 1% of the cell width, red when deeper than the target. It is
  made for inspecting overlaps up close, together with the `view` setting.

A full chamber has some 1750 cells, and a frame should take a millisecond or two, not tens. Two
habits keep drawing fast: cells are batched, so that a whole view is a handful of canvas paths
rather than thousands, and the per-frame buffers are reused, so that drawing allocates almost
nothing.

## What is shown

By default the view fits the whole chamber with a margin, including a strip of the feeding channel
below it. The chamber's cavity is a box from $(-50, 140)$ to $(50, 200)$, open at the bottom.

```{.typescript #render-view}
export const VIEW = { minX: -55, maxX: 55, minY: 133, maxY: 205 };
export interface ViewRect { minX: number; maxX: number; minY: number; maxY: number; }

const CHAMBER_BOX = { minX: -50, maxX: 50, minY: 140, maxY: 200 };
```

The options of a frame: the style, the cell radius, the area to show, and for the diagnostic view
the overlapping pairs (cell indices in `forEachCell` order, with their depths) and the depth above
which a pair is drawn in red.

```{.typescript #render-options}
export interface RenderOptions {
  style: RenderStyle;
  radius: number;
  view?: ViewRect;
  overlaps?: { i: Int32Array, j: Int32Array, depth: Float64Array, count: number };
  targetDepth?: number;
}
```

## Collecting the cells

At the start of each frame the renderer copies what it needs from the simulation into typed
arrays: each cell's centre and the half-axis vector $u = \tfrac{\ell}{2}(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)$,
so that the axis runs from $c - u$ to $c + u$. Each cell's colour is replaced by a small region
number, the index of that colour in a list of the colours seen so far, so that the diagnostic view
can draw each region in one path. The callback is created once, as a field, rather than on every
frame.

```{.typescript #render-buffers}
private n = 0;
private x = new Float64Array(0); private y = new Float64Array(0);
private ux = new Float64Array(0); private uy = new Float64Array(0);
private region = new Uint8Array(0);
private regionColors: RGB[] = [];
private readonly collect = (x: number, y: number, angle: number, length: number, color: RGB): void => {
  const k = this.n++;
  const h = length / 2;
  this.x[k] = x; this.y[k] = y;
  this.ux[k] = -Math.sin(angle) * h; this.uy[k] = Math.cos(angle) * h;
  let r = this.regionColors.indexOf(color);
  if (r < 0) { r = this.regionColors.length; this.regionColors.push(color); }
  this.region[k] = r;
};
```

The arrays grow when needed, at least doubling, and are reused otherwise:

```{.typescript #render-gather}
private gather(sim: Simulation): void {
  const n = sim.cellCount;
  if (this.x.length < n) {
    const m = Math.max(n, 2 * this.x.length, 1024);
    this.x = new Float64Array(m); this.y = new Float64Array(m);
    this.ux = new Float64Array(m); this.uy = new Float64Array(m);
    this.region = new Uint8Array(m);
  }
  this.n = 0;
  sim.forEachCell(this.collect);
}
```

## From world to screen

All drawing happens in world coordinates. One transform maps the view onto the canvas: it scales
the view to fit (keeping its proportions), centres it, and flips the $y$ axis, since the canvas's
$y$ points down and the world's points up. Line widths are therefore in world units; to draw a line
one pixel wide at any zoom, the drawing code divides by the scale. Round caps make a stroked
segment look like a capsule, which the cell drawing relies on.

```{.typescript #render-draw}
public draw(sim: Simulation, options: RenderOptions): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx, canvas = ctx.canvas;
  this.gather(sim);

  const v = options.view ?? VIEW;
  const scale = Math.min(canvas.width / (v.maxX - v.minX), canvas.height / (v.maxY - v.minY));
  const cx = (v.minX + v.maxX) / 2, cy = (v.minY + v.maxY) / 2;
  ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1;
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = "source-over";
  ctx.setTransform(scale, 0, 0, -scale, canvas.width / 2 - cx * scale, canvas.height / 2 + cy * scale);
  ctx.lineCap = "round";
  ctx.lineJoin = "round";

  switch (options.style) {
    case "simple": this.drawSimple(sim, scale, options.radius); break;
    case "diagnostic": this.drawDiagnostic(sim, scale, options); break;
  }
  ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
}
```

## The simple view

The walls and their triangles are drawn first. Then the cells, with a trick: tracing 1750 capsule
outlines with arcs took about 30 ms per frame. Instead, every cell's axis is stroked twice, as one
path each time: first dark and as wide as the cell, then white and one pixel narrower on each side.
What remains of the dark stroke is the outline, drawn just inside each cell, so two touching cells
both keep theirs. That takes about 1 ms.

Last come the anchors that hold a cell: a square at the anchor point and a line to the cell's
centre, all in one path, stroked and then filled (the lines have no area, so the fill only colours
the squares). Anchor points that hold nothing are not drawn here.

```{.typescript #render-simple}
private drawSimple(sim: Simulation, scale: number, radius: number): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx;
  this.clear("#ffffff");
  this.strokeWalls("#000000", 1.5 / scale, 0);
  this.strokeTriangles("#000000", 1 / scale);
  const line = 1 / scale;
  this.strokeCells(null, "#303030", 2 * radius);
  this.strokeCells(null, "#ffffff", Math.max(0, 2 * radius - 2 * line));
  const marker = 5 / scale;
  ctx.beginPath();
  sim.forEachAnchor((x, y, cell: Point | null) => {
    if (!cell) { return; }
    ctx.moveTo(x, y); ctx.lineTo(cell.x, cell.y);
    ctx.rect(x - marker / 2, y - marker / 2, marker, marker);
  });
  ctx.strokeStyle = ctx.fillStyle = "#d02020";
  ctx.lineWidth = line;
  ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fill();
}
```

## The diagnostic view

The material of the device (PDMS) is shaded, and the cells are filled region by region, one path
per colour. Their true outlines are drawn on top, so that a cell reaching into its neighbour shows
as a line crossing it.

The overlapping pairs passed in by the viewer are drawn as both cells' axes, in two passes: orange
for pairs below the target, then, thicker, red for those above it, so the worst ones are on top.
Finally all anchors are drawn, including those that hold nothing: springs as lines, anchor points
as black squares five pixels wide.

```{.typescript #render-diagnostic}
private drawDiagnostic(sim: Simulation, scale: number, options: RenderOptions): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx;
  const radius = options.radius;
  this.clear("#ffffff");
  this.fillPdms("#dfe6df");
  this.strokeWalls("#333", 2 / scale, 0);
  for (let r = 0; r < this.regionColors.length; r++) {
    const c = this.regionColors[r];
    this.strokeCells((k) => this.region[k] === r, `rgb(${255 * c.r},${255 * c.g},${255 * c.b})`, 2 * radius);
  }
  this.outlineCells(radius, "rgba(0,0,0,0.75)", 1 / scale);

  const o = options.overlaps;
  if (o) {
    for (const red of [false, true]) {
      ctx.beginPath();
      for (let p = 0; p < o.count; p++) {
        if ((o.depth[p] > (options.targetDepth ?? Infinity)) !== red) { continue; }
        for (const k of [o.i[p], o.j[p]]) {
          ctx.moveTo(this.x[k] - this.ux[k], this.y[k] - this.uy[k]);
          ctx.lineTo(this.x[k] + this.ux[k], this.y[k] + this.uy[k]);
        }
      }
      ctx.strokeStyle = red ? "#e00000" : "#ff9900";
      ctx.lineWidth = red ? 0.45 : 0.2;
      ctx.stroke();
    }
  }

  ctx.beginPath();
  sim.forEachAnchor((x, y, cell: Point | null) => {
    if (cell) { ctx.moveTo(x, y); ctx.lineTo(cell.x, cell.y); }
  });
  ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(0,0,0,0.6)";
  ctx.lineWidth = 1 / scale;
  ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle = "#000";
  const marker = 5 / scale;
  sim.forEachAnchor((x, y) => { ctx.fillRect(x - marker / 2, y - marker / 2, marker, marker); });
}
```

## Drawing primitives

### Cells

A cell is drawn by stroking its axis with round caps, at the cell's width: one `moveTo`/`lineTo`
pair per cell, and one `stroke` for all the selected cells together.

```{.typescript #render-stroke-cells}
private strokeCells(select: ((k: number) => boolean) | null, style: string, width: number): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx;
  ctx.beginPath();
  for (let k = 0; k < this.n; k++) {
    if (select && !select(k)) { continue; }
    const ux = this.ux[k], uy = this.uy[k];
    ctx.moveTo(this.x[k] - ux, this.y[k] - uy);
    ctx.lineTo(this.x[k] + ux, this.y[k] + uy);
  }
  ctx.strokeStyle = style;
  ctx.lineWidth = width;
  ctx.stroke();
}
```

The true outline of a capsule is two half circles joined by straight sides. With $\varphi$ the
direction from the centre to the end $c + u$, the path starts at the side of that end, runs around
it by a half circle, crosses (as a straight side) to the other end, runs around that, and closes
with the second straight side.

```{.typescript #render-outline-cells}
private outlineCells(radius: number, style: string, width: number): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx;
  ctx.beginPath();
  for (let k = 0; k < this.n; k++) {
    const x = this.x[k], y = this.y[k], ux = this.ux[k], uy = this.uy[k];
    const theta = Math.atan2(uy, ux);
    ctx.moveTo(x + ux + radius * Math.cos(theta - Math.PI / 2), y + uy + radius * Math.sin(theta - Math.PI / 2));
    ctx.arc(x + ux, y + uy, radius, theta - Math.PI / 2, theta + Math.PI / 2);
    ctx.arc(x - ux, y - uy, radius, theta + Math.PI / 2, theta + 3 * Math.PI / 2);
    ctx.closePath();
  }
  ctx.strokeStyle = style;
  ctx.lineWidth = width;
  ctx.stroke();
}
```

### Background and walls

The background is a rectangle somewhat larger than the default view:

```{.typescript #render-clear}
private clear(color: string): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx;
  ctx.fillStyle = color;
  ctx.fillRect(VIEW.minX - 10, VIEW.minY - 10, VIEW.maxX - VIEW.minX + 20, VIEW.maxY - VIEW.minY + 20);
}
```

The device material is everything except the cavity and the channel below it: three rectangles, to
the left of the chamber, to its right and above it, each reaching well beyond the view, plus the
wall triangles.

```{.typescript #render-pdms}
private fillPdms(color: string): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx, B = CHAMBER_BOX, far = 20;
  ctx.fillStyle = color;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.rect(VIEW.minX - far, B.minY, B.minX - VIEW.minX + far, VIEW.maxY - B.minY + far);
  ctx.rect(B.maxX, B.minY, VIEW.maxX - B.maxX + far, VIEW.maxY - B.minY + far);
  ctx.rect(B.minX, B.maxY, B.maxX - B.minX, VIEW.maxY - B.maxY + far);
  for (const t of CHAMBER.triangles) {
    const [a, b, c] = t.vertices;
    ctx.moveTo(a.x + t.offset.x, a.y + t.offset.y);
    ctx.lineTo(b.x + t.offset.x, b.y + t.offset.y);
    ctx.lineTo(c.x + t.offset.x, c.y + t.offset.y);
    ctx.closePath();
  }
  ctx.fill();
}
```

The outline of the device is one line: along the channel's upper edge from the left, up the left
wall, across the top, down the right wall and along the channel to the right. `inset` moves it into
the chamber (both views use 0).

```{.typescript #render-walls}
private strokeWalls(style: string, width: number, inset: number): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx, B = CHAMBER_BOX;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(VIEW.minX - 20, B.minY - inset);
  ctx.lineTo(B.minX + inset, B.minY - inset);
  ctx.lineTo(B.minX + inset, B.maxY - inset);
  ctx.lineTo(B.maxX - inset, B.maxY - inset);
  ctx.lineTo(B.maxX - inset, B.minY - inset);
  ctx.lineTo(VIEW.maxX + 20, B.minY - inset);
  ctx.strokeStyle = style;
  ctx.lineWidth = width;
  ctx.stroke();
}
```

```{.typescript #render-triangles}
private strokeTriangles(style: string, width: number): void {
  const ctx = this.ctx;
  ctx.beginPath();
  for (const t of CHAMBER.triangles) {
    const [a, b, c] = t.vertices;
    ctx.moveTo(a.x + t.offset.x, a.y + t.offset.y);
    ctx.lineTo(b.x + t.offset.x, b.y + t.offset.y);
    ctx.lineTo(c.x + t.offset.x, c.y + t.offset.y);
    ctx.closePath();
  }
  ctx.strokeStyle = style;
  ctx.lineWidth = width;
  ctx.stroke();
}
```
